title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees
abstract: arXiv:2611.29966v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered dense search, and (iii) expands top passages into contiguous, section-aware spans under a token budget, plus content-hash-gated delta ingestion to keep the index cheap to update. We evaluate on five public-domain books (113 chapter-localization queries) and on QuALITY and NovelQA (200K+ token novels). In-house, we find a seed-stable precision/ranking tradeoff: with section expansion off, hierarchical retrieval returns a higher fraction of chunks fr

translated_title: 面向长篇叙事文档的结构利用型层次化检索：一种以精度为导向的学习型抽象树替代方案
translated_abstract: 针对书籍长度文档的检索增强生成（RAG）需要在数万词元的文本中定位一小段连贯的段落。平面密集检索忽略了文档结构；而 RAPTOR 则通过递归聚类和使用语言模型进行摘要来构建层次结构。我们研究了一种利用文档原生结构的互补设计：一个两级检索器，它（i）通过对章节摘要采用 BM25+密集混合匹配来选择章节，（ii）运行经章节过滤的密集搜索，（iii）在词元预算约束下将排名靠前的段落扩展为连续的、感知章节结构的文本跨度，此外还采用内容哈希门控的增量摄取机制，以保持索引更新成本低廉。我们在五本公有领域书籍（113 个章节定位查询）以及 QuALITY 和 NovelQA（20 万+词元的小说）数据集上进行了评估。在内部测试中，我们发现了随随机种子稳定的精度/排序权衡：当关闭章节扩展时，层次化检索返回的片段中具有更高比例的……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出了一种利用文档原生章节结构的两级层次化检索方法，通过章节摘要混合匹配选择、章节过滤密集搜索和词元预算约束下的感知章节段落扩展，并辅以内容哈希门控的廉价增量索引更新，作为 RAPTOR 等学习型抽象树之外的精度导向替代方案，用于长篇叙事文档的检索增强生成。
en_tdlr: A two-level structure-exploiting hierarchical retriever—combining chapter-recap hybrid selection, chapter-filtered dense search, and token-budgeted section-aware passage expansion with cheap content-hash-gated delta indexing—is proposed as a precision-oriented alternative to learned abstraction trees like RAPTOR for retrieval-augmented generation over long narrative documents.
